rationale: The candidate has a coherent single massing rule: a square-ish block with a central carved void, legible in all views and not visibly colliding across views. The open-space figure is strong and the form is not merely boxy, so repair integrity and void publicness are decent. However, for a gymnasium the roof/section logic is weak: the diagram reads as an enclosed hollow object or courtyard mass rather than one clear long-span hall with subordinate support/bar hierarchy. The dominant gesture is also too abstract and inwardly symmetrical to communicate a gym’s span, structure, and daylight logic. The parcel/access cues are not available here, so no site response is credited. Overall this is visually coherent but fails the program hard gate because the visible section does not convincingly support the gymnasium brief.
